course_name: Spring Cloud Gateway for a Strangler-Fig Migration to GKE

nodes.description: Docker containers: images, Dockerfile basics, running and inspecting containers.
Comfort operating containerized infrastructure on GKE (clusters, containers running in them) prior to this course.
REST/HTTP fundamentals: verbs, status codes, request/response headers.
Spring Boot application development fundamentals (dependency injection, application context, common starters).
Stand up a Spring Cloud Gateway instance and deploy it to a GKE cluster so it is reachable and ready to route traffic.

At the gateway, mint a custom internal token that emulates the token format the legacy application already expects, and propagate it to downstream services, so legacy/backend code does not need to change immediately.
Configure path-based route splitting at the gateway so that /legacy/** paths reach the legacy system and new paths reach the migrated microservices.
Have the gateway participate in or initiate OpenTelemetry distributed tracing, propagating trace context across gateway, microservices, and the legacy system.
Validate incoming JWTs issued by Microsoft Entra ID at the gateway, and apply CORS so legitimate cross-origin browser clients are allowed through.
Building a container image for the Spring Cloud Gateway application (Dockerfile, build process) ready for cluster deployment.

persona_variant.variant: Authors/maintains the Dockerfile and application build for the gateway image.
Operates the image build/publish pipeline and container registry.

nodes.description: What CORS is and why browsers enforce it: origins, preflight requests, and which response headers a server must return to allow a cross-origin call.
Configuring CORS at the gateway (allowed origins, methods, headers) so browser-based clients can call routed services.

persona_variant.variant: Sets the CORS configuration in the gateway's code/config.
Verifies CORS behavior end-to-end against real client calls.

nodes.description: Writing a custom GlobalFilter/GatewayFilter in Spring Cloud Gateway: filter ordering in the reactive chain, and the WebFlux/reactive gotchas involved in mutating a request or response in-flight.
Distributed tracing concepts: traces, spans, and how trace context propagates across process boundaries via request headers.
Configuring the gateway to validate incoming JWTs issued by Microsoft Entra ID before a request is allowed to proceed: signature, issuer, audience, and expiry checks.

persona_variant.variant: Implements/configures the resource-server JWT validation on the gateway route.
Supplies and wires the Entra tenant/JWKS configuration values, and verifies accepted vs rejected requests.

nodes.description: The Spring Cloud Gateway route model: predicates and built-in filters, and how routes are declared/configured (Java DSL or YAML) to direct a request.

persona_variant.variant: Authors routes via the Java RouteLocator API or YAML configuration.
Reads and validates route configuration and the resulting traffic-split behavior, without authoring Java.

nodes.description: Deploying the containerized gateway onto the GKE cluster: applying manifests, exposing the service, and confirming it is reachable.

persona_variant.variant: Leads manifest authoring and the cluster deployment itself.
Understands the deployment shape well enough to debug and iterate on the running gateway.

nodes.description: Constructing a new JWT programmatically: choosing claims and signing a token, applied specifically to mapping validated Entra ID claims into a differently-shaped token.

depth_staging.note: Revisits JWT structure to construct a new, differently-shaped token from already-validated claims, instead of only validating one.

nodes.description: What a JWT is: header/claims/signature structure, and what it means to validate a token's signature and standard claims (exp, aud, iss).

depth_staging.note: Enough structure/claims/signature understanding to validate an incoming token.

nodes.description: Kubernetes deployment concepts applied to GKE: Deployments, Services, and Ingress, and how a containerized app is exposed on a cluster.
The exact structure/claims the legacy application currently expects in its authentication token, which the minted gateway token must emulate.
nodes.root_rationale: The legacy application's exact token shape is not detailed in the specs; it must be supplied by the client, so this node cannot be decomposed further from the current stores.

nodes.description: Implementing and verifying the concrete path-based route rules so that /legacy/** reaches the legacy system and every other configured path reaches the correct migrated microservice.

persona_variant.variant: Deploys the configuration and verifies traffic actually splits as intended.

nodes.description: How Microsoft Entra ID issues tokens via OAuth2/OIDC: tenant, app registration, issuer, and the JWKS endpoint used to fetch signing keys.

persona_variant.variant: Consumes issuer/JWKS values inside validation code.
Configures the Entra app registration and supplies tenant/JWKS values.

nodes.description: Setting up the OpenTelemetry collector pipeline that receives traces emitted by the gateway and downstream services, so a full trace can be observed end-to-end.

persona_variant.variant: Deploys and operates the OTel collector pipeline.
Understands the pipeline enough to interpret traces while debugging.

nodes.description: Configuring/instrumenting the gateway to participate in OpenTelemetry tracing: propagating, and where needed initiating, trace context across the request to microservices and the legacy system.

persona_variant.variant: Adds/verifies OTel instrumentation in the gateway's code path.
Wires the OTel exporter configuration on the gateway deployment.

nodes.description: Using path-based predicates to split traffic: routing /legacy/** to the legacy system and other paths to migrated microservices.
What Spring Cloud Gateway is: its role as an edge reverse-proxy/API gateway sitting in front of both legacy and newly-migrated services.
The strangler-fig migration pattern: incrementally routing traffic to new microservices while the legacy system keeps serving the rest, so both environments coexist during the migration window.
nodes.root_rationale: The problem framing that motivates the whole course; it rests on no prior knowledge, so nothing is prerequisite to it.

nodes.description: Implementing gateway logic that mints a new internal token shaped like the legacy application's expected token, populated from the validated incoming Entra ID JWT's claims.

Propagating the minted internal token to downstream microservices and the legacy system by rewriting the outgoing request (e.g. replacing/adding the Authorization header) before it leaves the gateway.

edges.reason: The gateway is only "deployed" once it is running on the GKE cluster, which is exactly what this prerequisite covers.
Minting the token is only useful once it is propagated downstream; propagation is the last teachable step this objective requires.
The objective is exactly the concrete implementation of the legacy-vs-new path split.
A gateway emitting traces is only useful if a collector pipeline exists to receive them.
The gateway must be instrumented to participate in/initiate tracing before the objective is met.
The objective explicitly includes applying CORS at the gateway.
The objective explicitly includes validating incoming JWTs at the gateway.
Building a container image assumes basic Docker/Dockerfile fluency.
You need to know what the gateway application is before packaging it into an image.
CORS is a browser/HTTP-level mechanism, so it assumes basic REST/HTTP understanding.
You must understand what CORS is and why it exists before configuring it correctly.
CORS is applied through the gateway's route/filter configuration model.
Writing a custom GlobalFilter/GatewayFilter in Java requires Spring Boot fluency.
Custom filters extend the same route/filter model, so the general model must be understood first.
Trace context propagates via HTTP headers, so it assumes basic REST/HTTP understanding.
JWT validation is wired into the route/filter model, so that model must be understood first.
Validating a JWT requires knowing what a JWT is and what "valid" means for its structure and claims.
Validation depends on Entra-specific issuer/JWKS details from the OIDC flow.
The route/predicate/filter model is a detail of Spring Cloud Gateway, which must first be understood as a concept.
You must have a container image of the gateway before it can be deployed to the cluster.
Deploying to GKE requires knowing the Kubernetes deployment concepts (Deployment/Service/Ingress) being applied.
Constructing a token is a deeper pass over the same JWT structure already introduced at pass 1.
The claims being remapped into the new token come from the validated Entra-issued token, so the Entra OIDC flow must already be understood.
JWTs are carried in HTTP headers, so basic REST/HTTP understanding is assumed.
Kubernetes deployment concepts build on the container fundamentals learners already hold.
You must understand path-based route splitting conceptually before implementing the concrete legacy-vs-new rules.
OIDC issues and describes JWTs, so basic JWT structure must be understood first.
Setting up a collector pipeline assumes understanding what traces/spans are and why they need to be collected.
Instrumenting the gateway assumes understanding traces, spans, and context propagation first.
Tracing instrumentation is wired into the same route/filter model.
Path-based predicates are a specific use of the general route/predicate/filter model.
Splitting traffic by path is only motivated once the strangler-fig migration pattern it serves is understood.
Understanding a gateway as a reverse-proxy assumes basic REST/HTTP understanding.
The minting logic is implemented as a custom GlobalFilter, so custom filter authoring must be understood first.
The incoming Entra JWT must already be validated before its claims can be trusted and remapped.
Minting a token requires the deeper pass on JWT construction, not just validation.
The minted token must emulate the legacy application's expected format, so that format must be known first.
There must be a minted token before it can be propagated downstream.
